scope: Proposition B.1 (Four radial cap choices) of the manuscript “Finite triangular approximation of radial sweeps” (preprints/Finite-triangular-approximation-of-radial-sweeps-September-27-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 100 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6e7f63022190f390), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the tetrahedron and paired sweeps just described, each of the following caps gives coverage for every sufficiently small ε > 0: Rε(r) = 1 + ε2 (H(r) + β), β > 0, (L) Rε(r) = 1 + ε2 H(r) + cε3 , c ≥ 9/2, (C) Rε(r) = 1 + ε2 H(r) + cε5/2 , c > 0, (F) Rε(r) = q 1 + 2ε2(H(r) + β), β > 0. (S) For (C), coverage in fact holds for every ε > 0. Their normalized costs have the respective expansions QR(ε) = 1 + (2β − 1/30)ε2 + O(ε4 ), (L), (S), (B.2) QR(ε) = 1 − ε2 /30 + 2cε3 + O(ε4 ), (C), (B.3) QR(ε) = 1 − ε2 /30 + 2cε5/2 + O(ε4 ), (F). (B.4) Thus (L) and (S) give strict saving when 0 < β < 1/60; (C) and (F) give strict saving for every stated fixed c. In each case one first fixes a tilt giving coverage and strict saving, and then chooses a finite sufficiently fine partition.
